national_raw_news.title: 48 mins ago | National 45 166 Indian nationals rescued so far, 275 still missing; Indian govt in touch with Nepali govt: MEA
national_raw_news.content: The External Affairs Ministry today said that 166 Indian nationals have been rescued in Nepal so far after flash floods hit the neighbouring nation. Briefing media in New Delhi today, Spokesperson in the Ministry of External Affairs, Randhir Jaiswal said, 275 Indian nationals remain missing. He said, India continue to be in close touch with the Nepali government. He said, India deeply appreciates the efforts of the Nepalese authorities in this regard. The Spokesperson said, the Ministry has been regularly releasing the names of Indians who have been rescued. Mr Jaiswal said, one thousand 907 Indian nationals have safely crossed into Nepal from China. He said, there are no Indian travelers who are stranded in the Tibetan Autonomous Region in China. Regarding India’s support to flood ravaged Nepal, Mr Jaiswal said, India will continue to provide assistance as per the requirements of the Government of Nepal. He said, in the coming days India is planning to send more forensic kits, Bailey bridges, and other materials that are requested by the government of Nepal. On the remarks of Nepal Foreign Minister, Mr Jaiswal said, India has consistently maintained that climate change is a common challenge, and action in this regard must be based on the principle of common differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities. He said, developed countries who historically are responsible for the emissions and have contributed overwhelmingly to the civil crisis, must take lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries by way of finance and technology transfer to meet this challenge. On a media query on External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar’s visit to Ukraine, the Spokesperson said, Dr Jaishankar visited Kyiv and met with his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha and called on President Zelenskyy. He said, during his conversations, the External Affairs Minister noted that India has consistently maintained that this is not an era of war and that the solution will not emerge from the battlefield. He also underlined Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s comments that endless war must now give way to the end of war, noting that this is that it is for the parties involved to find a way. Mr Jaiswal said, the visit of Dr Jaishankar was focused on exploring the prospects of dialogue and diplomacy. He said, India’s national interest guides the energy purchases and the imperative for it is to meet the energy requirements of 1.4 billion people. On the Greater Malé Connectivity Project, Mr Jaiswal said, India is a leading development partner for the Maldives. He said, India have undertaken several projects in the country, which continue to bring a lot of value to the people of the Maldives. He added that the Greater Malé Connectivity Project is a project that connects the capital, Malé, with three islands and the first segment of the Project has been completed. On a Tamil Nadu woman named Vanitha who was rescued after a desperate SOS from Kuwait, Mr Jaiswal said, when the Indian embassy came to know of the issue, they gave her a helping hand and as of now, she is with the embassy. He said, Ministry of External Affairs remain committed to doing its best for the well-being, safety, and welfare of Indian nationals abroad. On the comments of the Mayor of Birmingham, Zaker Choudhry, regarding Kashmir, he said that the whole of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts India.

national_raw_news.title: 53 mins ago | National 473 Janmashtami being celebrated with religious faith and fervour across the country.
national_raw_news.content: The festival of Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna is being observed across the country with religious fervour today. On the occasion, devotees observe fast, perform ceremonies and visit temples. Sweets and other foods associated with Krishna are prepared and offered to Lord Krishna. Devotional songs and chanting is performed through the day and often late into the night. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have extended their greetings on the occasion of Janmashtami. In Gujarat, grand celebrations and special religious rituals are underway at major Krishna shrines including the world-famous Dwarkadhish, Dakor, and Shamalaji temples. In Uttar Pradesh, the streets of Mathura and Vrindavan are reverberating with the chanting of Jay Shri Krishna. All temples are decked up with flowers petals and colorful lights for midnight celebration. In Kerala, prominent Shri Krishna temples across the state witnessed a massive footfall of devotees from early morning hours. Special rituals were performed starting in the early morning at Shri Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram and at Guruvayur Sree Krishna Temple. Janmashtami is also being celebrated with religious fervour and devotion at various places across Kashmir. In Srinagar, Kashmiri Pandits took out a procession from Ganpatyar Temple in Habba Kadal to Lal Chowk. Devotees, including men, women and children, participated in the celebrations amid chanting of devotional slogans and bhajans.

national_raw_news.title: Meghalaya witnesses over 11000 runners of national and international stature in Half Marathon 2026 2 hours ago 43
national_raw_news.content: The 5th Sohra International Half Marathon 2026 was successfully held today, bringing together regional, national, and international athletes to Meghalaya. The event was organised by the Meghalaya State Olympics Association (MSOA) in collaboration with the Directorate of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya, Meghalaya Athletics Association and an official recognised by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI). The 2026 edition saw the registration of 11,672 runners across all categories. Participation included international athletes and runners from other states as well. In his keynote address,Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister, Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya highlighted the event’s remarkable evolution from a modest starting field of 750 runners to nearly 12,000 participants. Welcoming athletes representing almost 24 states across the country, Shylla emphasized the marathon’s widespread socio-economic impact, which directly benefits local homestay operators, transport providers, and farmers, while establishing Sohra as a top-tier sporting destination beyond its traditional fame for rain and waterfalls. Sukant Suki Singh, the first Indian to Complete three 200-Mile Ultramarathons, praised Meghalaya’s exceptional sports infrastructure and natural beauty, identifying the state as the future sporting capital of India. He specifically commended Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma for completely transforming the region’s sports landscape and actively nurturing athletic talent from a young age. The Sohra Half Marathon witnessed strong performances across all its competitive categories, with Satish Kumar Verma emerging winner in the Elite Men’s 21 km category with a timing of 1:03:04, and Tejaswini Narendra Lambkane claiming the Elite Women’s title in 1:15:20.

national_raw_news.title: Drass District Festival showcases immense tourism potential of the region 1 hour ago 35
national_raw_news.content: In Ladakh, the first-ever Drass District Festival 2026 was inaugurated today by Deputy Commissioner Drass, Kacho Imtiyaz Ahmed, marking a historic occasion for the newly established district. The two-day festival aims to showcase the rich culture, traditions, heritage, natural beauty and immense tourism potential of Drass. The festival commenced with a guided Nature Trail to promote eco-tourism, environmental awareness and wildlife conservation. The programme highlighted the fragile ecosystem of the Drass and Mushkoh valleys, with special focus on the conservation of the endangered Himalayan Brown Bear and protection of its natural habitat. Various activities, including nature tours, Horse Polo, exhibitions, cultural programmes and stalls showcasing local products and traditions, are being organised as part of the festival. Speaking on the occasion, Deputy Commissioner Drass Kacho Imtiyaz Ahmed emphasised the importance of promoting Drass as a destination for cultural, eco and adventure tourism, while ensuring the preservation of its unique environment and rich heritage. The festival is also providing an important platform for local artists, youth, artisans, tourism stakeholders and communities to showcase their talent, products and traditions. The celebrations highlight the message that Drass is not only a land of history and courage, but also a destination of culture, nature and adventure, with immense potential for sustainable tourism.
